method_limits: a literal is counted when some string constant's last path component equals the basename; a literal split across os.path.join arguments is not reconstructed here (E422 owns join-chain reconstruction), so faces named only that way land in the C_NONE bucket rather than C_LITERAL.

specificity is text-level: a template is specific when a fragment keeps a non-empty stem after the last '/' and the '.json' suffix are removed. A template like '%s.json' that receives a literal stem through a variable is therefore discarded here even though it does name a face at runtime -- the discard list is published.

in_an_opener is the nearest enclosing FunctionDef containing any call to a name in OPENERS; it is not dataflow. A name built in a function that also logs an unrelated file counts as being in an opener.
the corpus is source text on disk; a module that does not parse contributes nothing (half-written scratch files are common in this tree).
this study's own file is excluded by name (E180/E207 family), so its templates and literals cannot feed the reading.

rows and templates move when any module is added or edited -- a new collector with a new literal legitimately reclassifies a face. The producer must be re-derived after the corpus grows (E421/E419 precedent); verify therefore compares rows, not counts.
the population excludes basenames starting with '_': those are round receipts and scratch faces that every round rewrites, so counting them would move the reading without moving the tree's content.
